There is controversy as to the risk formalde- hyde presents as a carcinogen. Studies on the occupational expo- sure of medical personnel and industrial workers1-3 to formalde- hyde have generally concluded that although the risk is small or non-existent, the possibility that formaldehyde is a human car- cinogen cannot be excluded. Reanalyses of some studies have led to different interpretations of the results, with some workers concluding that the risk of cancer from formaldehyde is greater than originally thought.4 Analysis of mortality data5 for a cohort of 25619 workers exposed to formaldehyde in the USA found some evidence of an association with nasopharyngeal cancer and possibly cancers at other upper respiratory-tract sites.
